chunks: From him, from Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from al-Dahhak ibn al-Ash'ath, from Dawud ibn Zarbi, who said:

I brought some wealth to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him). He took some of it and left some of it. I said: May God rectify you, why did you leave it with me? He said: The one who holds this authority will ask for it from you. When his obituary arrived, Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) sent for me and asked me for that wealth, and I handed it over to him.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا: Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (Title of Imam Musa ibn Ja'far)
key_terms.أَبِي إِبۡرَاهِيمَ: Abu Ibrahim (Title of Imam Musa al-Kadim)
key_terms.صَاحِبَ الْأَمۡرِ: The one in charge of the authority (Referring to the succeeding Imam)

ai.seo_question: What is the story of the wealth left with Imam al-Kadim and reclaimed by Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the continuity of the Imamate by showing Imam Musa al-Kadhim explicitly designating his son, Ali al-Rida, as the successor to hold specific trusts. The act of reclaiming the funds upon al-Kadim's death serves as a practical demonstration of the transfer of authority (wilayah) and financial stewardship, reinforcing the legitimacy of al-Rida’s imamate in the eyes of his followers.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 18 - It is narrated from Ahmad bin Mehran from Muhammad bin Ali from Zahak bin Ashath from Dawood bin Zarbi  that he said:

I brought some money to Abu Ibrahim [Imam Musa Kadhim (a.s)]. He took some of it and left some of it. “May God set you right,” I said, “Why have you left it with me?” “The one who will be in charge of the authority will ask you for it,”  he told. When the news of his death came, Abul Hasan, Ridha (a.s) summoned me and asked me for that money and I paid it to him.
